reasoning: This is a load-bearing flange/bracket: it holds a 2 kg shelf in bending on the flange and is screwed through the plate. The load path runs from the shelf, through the flange (bending: compression on top, tension on bottom), through the plate at the screw holes (shear/compression), down to the mounting surface. The 4.76 mm section gives a solid cross-section, but at the preset's 15% zig-zag infill the core is mostly void, and the walls at only 2 loops leave most of the section as weak infill at the very surfaces where bending stress peaks. No overhangs, no bridges, no supports needed. Bed contact is generous (1800 mm²), slenderness is low (1.5×), so no adhesion or wobble concern.

changes.reason: The flange carries the 2 kg shelf in bending, so the outer surfaces (where walls sit) are where bending stress peaks. Two loops gives roughly 0.9 mm of solid wall in a 4.76 mm section; four gives roughly 1.9 mm, putting more load-bearing material at the high-stress surfaces.

Under the bending load the bottom of the flange is in tension — the side where failure initiates in PLA. Three layers at 0.2 mm gives 0.6 mm solid; five gives 1.0 mm, matching the top shell and giving the tension-critical surface more solid material.
The part holds a 2 kg shelf; 15% leaves the 4.76 mm section mostly void between the walls. Raising to 40% adds shear and stiffness to the core without making the part solid.
The shelf can load the flange in any horizontal direction, so strength must be equal in all directions. Zig-zag has Low Z strength per the wiki table; gyroid has High in both X-Y and Z.
The load path depends on layer bonding at the outer walls, which carry the bending stress. Slowing from 160 to 120 improves adhesion between wall layers.
Same load-path reasoning: layer bonding through the inner walls contributes to the flange's bending strength. Keeping inner walls well clear of the volumetric limit reduces internal stress.
The load path depends on layer bonding. The wiki says toward the warmer end for load-bearing parts; 230 is within the 190–240 range and gives better inter-layer adhesion without risking degradation.

design_notes: No overhang (0 mm², 0° steepest) and no bridge (0 mm²), so no supports are needed and no design-out chamfer applies.
Bed contact of 1800 mm² and slenderness of 1.5× are both well within safe limits; no brim or adhesion change is warranted.
